reasoning: The problem's components are all well-established but the specific measured question is unexplored. SHADE-Arena provides ground-truth harmful side-task steps and whole-trajectory monitor AUC (0.87); turn-by-turn monitoring (SHADE-Arena, Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring) already assigns per-step suspicion and documents failure modes like "long-horizon deferral" where the attack hides in final steps; and defer-to-trusted/resampling protocols (Ctrl-Z, Evaluating Control Protocols) operationally depend on per-step suspicion localizing to the harmful action. The TRACE framework (arXiv 2504/researchgate) explicitly identifies "high-signal regions" within SHADE-Arena trajectories but synthesizes a trajectory-level verdict (F1 0.713) rather than scoring whether suspicion ranks the true harmful step top-1/top-k/MRR. TrajAD does step-level localization but for benign execution errors on AgentBank, not safety sabotage, and uses Joint Exact Match. No found work directly computes the rank of the known side-task step in per-step suspicion ordering and contrasts that localization metric against whole-trajectory AUC, so the specific angle (validating the localization assumption that step-level deferral relies on) is novel, while the building blocks and implicit assumption are heavily covered.

evidence.title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Provides the malign/benign transcripts with known harmful side-task steps and whole-trajectory monitor AUC (0.87 for Gemini 2.5 Pro). Discusses turn-by-turn monitoring (max suspicion over recent turns) and a 'long-horizon deferral' false-negative pattern, but reports trajectory-level detection, not per-step localization rank against the true harmful step.

evidence.title: TRACE: Trajectory Reasoning through Adaptive Cross-Step Evidence Aggregation for LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Closest work: a Triage-Inspect-Judge monitor on ten SHADE-Arena domains that identifies high-signal regions but produces a trajectory-level verdict (F1 0.713, recall 0.844). Does not measure whether suspicion localizes to the ground-truth harmful step via top-1/top-k/MRR, nor contrast localization with whole-trajectory AUC.

evidence.title: TrajAD: Trajectory Anomaly Detection for Trustworthy LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Does precise step-level localization of errors with ground-truth step indices, but targets general execution reliability anomalies (task failure, inefficiency, unwarranted continuation) on AgentBank, not safety sabotage; uses Joint Exact Match rather than ranking metrics. Demonstrates step localization is a known capability but in a non-safety setting.

evidence.title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Studies turn-by-turn/aggregated per-step suspicion scoring and aggregation functions; notes false-negative patterns where deceptive actions concentrate in final steps. Implicitly relevant to whether suspicion localizes but evaluated via detection rates, not rank of the true harmful step.

evidence.title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
evidence.summary: Defer/resample-to-trusted protocols act on the most suspicious step, operationally assuming per-step suspicion localizes to the harmful action. This assumption is exactly what the proposal tests but is not directly validated here.
